extracted.intended_audience: general public, researchers, and practitioners seeking summaries of U.S. federal agency missions, authorities, and program rules
extracted.subtask_description: Directory-style summaries of U.S. federal agencies that state statutory duties, program authorities, procedural limits, and quality or governance standards as presented on a Federal Register agencies listing page.

rubrics_metrics.name: BLS data quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: BLS data must satisfy a number of criteria, including relevance to current social and economic issues, timeliness in reflecting today’s rapidly changing economic conditions, accuracy and consistently high statistical quality, and impartiality in both subject matter and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFIUS review national-security focus (Investment Security Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: CFIUS is an interagency committee that can review certain foreign investments in the United States in order to identify and address any effects on U.S. national security that may arise from the transactions. The CFIUS review process ... focuses solely on national security concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operates in the context of the United States’ longstanding open investment policy; Treasury (Investment Security Office) implements Treasury’s responsibilities as Chair of CFIUS and leads related open investment initiatives and dialogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and enrollment for actuaries (Joint Board for Enrollment of Actuaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Board shall, by regulations, establish reasonable standards and qualifications for persons performing actuarial services with respect to plans in which this chapter applies and, upon application by any individual, shall enroll such individual if the Joint Board finds that such individual satisfies such standards and qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis: 29 U.S.C. 1242; the Board sets regulatory standards and enrollment is contingent on satisfying those standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Television Loan Guarantee Program limits and expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board is authorized to approve Guarantees up to 80 percent of the principal amount of up to $1.25 billion in Loans. The Board's authority to guarantee Loans under the Program expires on the earlier of the date the Secretary of Agriculture determines that at least 75 percent of Designated Market Areas, other than the top 40 DMAs, have access to Local Television Broadcast Signals for virtually all households or December 31, 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program purpose: to facilitate access, on a technologically neutral basis, to signals of local television stations for households located in non-served or underserved areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Joint Commission functions for transboundary waters
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Joint Commission rules upon applications for approval of projects affecting boundary or transboundary waters and may regulate the operation of these projects; it assists the two countries in the protection of the transboundary environment, including the implementation of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement and the improvement of transboundary air quality; and it alerts the governments to emerging issues along the boundary that may give rise to bilateral disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established by the Boundary Waters Treaty of 1909; acts as an independent binational organization advising the U.S. and Canada and exercising regulatory/review functions for transboundary projects and environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Conference statutory responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 331 of title 28 specifically provides that the Judicial Conference shall: (1) Make a comprehensive survey of the conditions of business in the courts of the United States; (2) Prepare plans for the assignment of judges to or from courts of appeals or district courts, where necessary; (3) Submit suggestions to the various courts in the interest of promoting uniformity of management procedures and the expeditious conduct of court business; (4) Exercise authority provided in chapter 16 of title 28 United States Code for the review of circuit council conduct and disability orders filed under that chapter; and (5) Carry on a continuous study of the operation and effect of the general rules of practice and procedure in use within the federal courts, as prescribed by the Supreme Court pursuant to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Conference also supervises the Director of the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts in the performance of his duties as the administrative officer of the courts of the United States under 28 U.S.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review standards for loyalty determinations (International Organizations Employees Loyalty Board)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of the Board was to review cases referred to it under the provisions of EO 10422, in which the loyalty of U.S. citizens either employed or considered for employment by international organizations whose membership included the United States was in question. The Board ... was to make advisory determinations in such cases, under the standards set forth elsewhere in the Executive Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board composed of not less than three impartial officers or employees of OPM; determinations are advisory and governed by EO 10422 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: LMRDA standards for labor organizations (origin of OLMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act of 1959 (LMRDA) was enacted by Congress to ensure certain basic standards of democracy and fiscal responsibility in labor organizations representing employees in private industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LMRDA established statutory standards that the current Office of Labor-Management Standards traces to; OLMS duties historically flow from ensuring those democracy and fiscal responsibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: USITC commissioner appointment and composition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Six Commissioners are appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate for 9-year terms, unless appointed to fill an unexpired term. The Chairman and Vice Chairman are designated by the President for 2-year terms, and succeeding Chairmen may not be of the same political party. Not more than three Commissioners may be members of the same political party (19 U.S.C. 1330).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission furnishes studies, reports, and recommendations involving international trade and conducts investigations pertaining to international trade relief; its composition and appointment rules are statutory constraints intended to ensure independence and bipartisanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Japan-U.S. Friendship Commission grant-decision composition and process
rubrics_metrics.description: A board of 18 Commissioners makes decisions on the expenditure of JUSFC’s earnings. The Commissioners are a group of nine private citizens and nine U.S. government officials who meet annually to consider all institutional grant proposals submitted to JUSFC. Among the government officials are four bi-partisan Members of the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives who serve in a non-voting capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-making is annual and institutional grant proposals are considered by a mixed board of private and government members; funding comes from a trust fund rather than general revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Television Loan Guarantee Program eligibility purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the provisions of the act, the Board was authorized to guarantee loans to facilitate access, on a technologically neutral basis, to signals of local television stations for households located in non-served areas or underserved areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design is targeted to increase access in non-served/underserved DMAs; guarantees limited as described (see program limits entry).
